name: Leave for victims of violence against women and their children
authority: Republic Act 9262 (Anti-Violence Against Women and Their Children Act of 2004) sec. 43 RA 9262 s.43 grants it to a woman employee; an unrecorded `employee.gender` offers none until recorded. RA 9262 s.43: up to ten days; an entry over ten days is refused. Metered per event (`window: EVENT`).

name: Paternity leave
eligibility: employee.gender == "MALE" && employee.marital_status == "MARRIED" && has(entry.event_kind) && entry.event_kind in ["BIRTH", "MISCARRIAGE"] && (!has(entry.days) || entry.days <= 7.0 + (has(entry.facts.maternity_days_allocated) ? min(double(entry.facts.maternity_days_allocated), 7.0) : 0.0)) && size(earlier.rows.filter(r, (has(r.facts.event_id) ? r.facts.event_id : r.id) != (has(entry.facts) && has(entry.facts.event_id) ? entry.facts.event_id : "") && !earlier.rows.exists(s, (has(s.facts.event_id) ? s.facts.event_id : s.id) == (has(r.facts.event_id) ? r.facts.event_id : r.id) && (s.occurred_on < r.occurred_on || (s.occurred_on == r.occurred_on && s.id < r.id))))) < 4
authority: Republic Act 8187 sec. 3 seven days per delivery of the legitimate spouse, for the first four (RA 8187 s.2; `lifetime_events`). RA 8187 s.2: seven days for the delivery of, or miscarriage by, the legitimate spouse (`event.kind in [BIRTH, MISCARRIAGE]`), the first four deliveries; s.4? the leave is not convertible to cash. RA 8187 s.2 grants it to a married male employee for his lawful wife's delivery; an unrecorded `employee.gender` or `employee.marital_status` offers no paternity leave until recorded — the grant's conditions, never a default. RA 8187 s.2: seven days to a married male employee for each of the first four deliveries (live birth or miscarriage) of his lawful wife; the entry states `event_kind`; an entry over seven days is refused. Metered per delivery (`window: EVENT`). RA 8187 s.2: for the first four deliveries — the eligibility counts the earlier deliveries (distinct `facts.event_id` of the employment’s earlier paternity entries, `earlier.rows`) and refuses a fifth; the seven days meter per delivery (the EVENT window’s default key, `facts.event_id`; an entry without one is its own delivery). RA 11210 s.6: the mother may allocate up to seven of her maternity days to the father (entry fact `maternity_days_allocated`, customer input), raising this leave to fourteen.

name: Special leave for women (gynaecological surgery)
authority: Republic Act 9710 (Magna Carta of Women) sec. 18 with DOLE Department Order 112-A s.2012 two months per gynaecological surgery (RA 9710 s.18; `event.kind == "SURGERY"`), after six months’ aggregate service in the twelve before it (read as six months’ service). RA 9710 s.18 grants it to a woman employee; an unrecorded `employee.gender` offers none until recorded. RA 9710 s.18: up to two months after gynaecological surgery, after six months of service in the last twelve; the entry states `event_kind: SURGERY`. Up to 60 days per surgery (Handbook leave table item 6), metered per event.

name: Annual leave
authority: Labor Code of the Philippines (P.D. 442, as amended) art.95 Art.95(2) and Handbook ch.7 §B: service incentive leave does not reach field personnel, workers on task, contract or purely commission basis, domestic helpers, or an establishment regularly employing fewer than ten (`company.facts.small_establishment`). RA 10361 s.29: a kasambahay of one year’s service has the five days of service incentive leave too; the Labor Code art.95 exclusion of domestic workers is overtaken. DOLE Handbook on Workers’ Statutory Monetary Benefits (2023) ch.7 §D: the use and conversion “may be on a pro rata basis”, and its illustration — hired 1 January 2022, resigned 1 March 2023 — converts 5 days earned as of 31 December 2022 plus (2/12) × 5 = 0.833 for January and February 2023, 5.833 in all, unrounded. The year's five days are therefore earned by completed months of the leave year and never rounded (`COMPLETED_MONTHS`, `EXACT`); a year of whole service still holds all five from its start. Coverage (§B) checked against the Handbook: government, personal service (overtaken for the kasambahay by RA 10361 s.29, `ANNUAL_LEAVE_DOMESTIC`), managerial employees and managerial staff (`MANAGERIAL`), field personnel and the unsupervised, including those on task or contract, purely commission or fixed-amount basis (Omnibus Rules Book III Rule V s.1(d); `FIELD_PERSONNEL`, `TASK_BASIS`) — a supervised piece-rate worker (`PIECE_RATE`) is not excluded, and establishments regularly employing fewer than ten (`small_establishment`) are outside; those already enjoying the benefit or five days' vacation leave with pay hold it through the employer's own leave row, which this statutory row does not duplicate. Omnibus Rules Implementing the Labor Code Book III Rule V s.5: service incentive leave not used or exhausted at the end of the year is commutable to its money equivalent; the year-end conversion is raised by its schedule on the leave year’s last day for the unused days. Metered per service year (`window: SERVICE_YEAR`), no carry-forward: unused days are commuted at the year end (Omnibus Rules Book III Rule V s.5). At the end of each service year the untaken balance is paid automatically: `encash_at_window_end` — the daily tick writes one ENCASHMENT movement for the balance on the window’s last day (once), priced by the ENCASHMENT work line at the daily rate in the period holding that day. Omnibus Rules Book III Rule V s.5 (https://elibrary.judiciary.gov.ph/thebookshelf/showdocs/2/85819, read 2026-10-08): service incentive leave "shall be commutable to its money equivalent if not used or exhausted at the end of the year". The first service year earns nothing, so nothing is paid at its end. A kasambahay’s ANNUAL_LEAVE_DOMESTIC is not encashed: RA 10361 s.29 — "Unused leaves shall not be convertible to cash".

entitlement.days: size(bands.filter(b, service_months >= b.service_months).map(b, b.days)) > 0 ? first(bands.filter(b, service_months >= b.service_months).map(b, b.days)) : 0.0

name: Maternity leave
eligibility: employee.gender == "FEMALE" && has(entry.event_kind) && (entry.event_kind == "BIRTH" ? (!has(entry.days) || entry.days <= ((has(entry.facts) && has(entry.facts.solo_parent_claimed) ? entry.facts.solo_parent_claimed : employee.solo_parent) ? 120.0 : 105.0)) : entry.event_kind in ["MISCARRIAGE", "EMERGENCY_TERMINATION"] && (!has(entry.days) || entry.days <= 60.0))
authority: Republic Act 11210 secs. 3 and 5: a pregnant private-sector female worker receives 105 days of maternity leave with full pay for a live birth, 60 days for miscarriage or emergency termination, and an additional 15 days if qualified as a solo parent. Section 5(a) separately requires three paid SSS contributions in the twelve months before the contingency semester for the SSS cash benefit. Months since SSS registration do not establish that contribution history and do not gate this leave entitlement. The SSS advance, reimbursement and employer salary differential require separate assessment under sec. 5(c). RA 11861 secs. 15 and 20 govern the Solo Parent Identification Card; unrecorded gender is not presumed, and the fifteen solo-parent days need the birth's benefit case to prove the claim with an event-valid LGU document (payroll.benefit_cases:MATERNITY_LEAVE, qualification solo_parent_documented), not the employee's current flag. An event entered as EMERGENCY_TERMINATION receives the same 60-day branch as miscarriage under RA 11210 secs. 3 and 5 and the implementing rules; this is a distinct event kind, not inferred from a live birth. The entry states the event in its facts (`event_kind`: BIRTH, MISCARRIAGE or EMERGENCY_TERMINATION); an entry over 105 days (120 for a solo parent) or 60 days is refused. Metered per event (`entry.facts.event_id`): 105 days, 120 for a solo parent; the 60-day limit for a miscarriage or emergency termination is the eligibility’s per-entry cap. Each pregnancy (`window_key`: `facts.event_id`) is its own balance: 60 days when its first entry is a miscarriage or emergency termination, else 105 (120 solo parent). RA 11210 s.6: up to seven of the days may be allocated to the child’s father or an alternate caregiver (entry fact `days_allocated_to_father`, customer input) and are deducted here; the solo-parent 15 days follow the event’s own `solo_parent_claimed` (RA 11861), else the current flag.

name: Parental leave for solo parents
authority: Republic Act 8972 (Solo Parents' Welfare Act) sec. 8 as amended by Republic Act 11861 (Expanded Solo Parents Welfare Act) RA 8972 as amended by RA 11861 s.8: seven days a year, non-cumulative and non-convertible (an UPFRONT grant with no carry), on a valid Solo Parent ID card (`evidence: REQUIRED`). solo-parent standing is what the Solo Parent Identification Card establishes (RA 11861 ss.15, 20: the benefit is availed on presenting the SPIC the local social welfare office issues); `employee.solo_parent` is false until the employer records a presented card, the statute's own default. RA 11861 s.8: after six months of service; an entry over seven days is refused (the yearly grant is not metered: the leave entitlement has no calendar-year reset). Metered per calendar year (`window: CALENDAR_YEAR`), forfeitable and noncumulative (RA 11861 s.6, https://elibrary.judiciary.gov.ph/thebookshelf/showdocs/2/95472).

name: Service incentive leave (kasambahay)
authority: RA 10361 (Batas Kasambahay) s.29: a kasambahay of one year’s service is entitled to five days of service incentive leave with pay; unused leave is not cumulative, not carried over and not convertible to cash. RA 10361 s.29: five days a year after a year of service, unused days neither cumulative nor convertible — metered per service year.

entitlement.days: size(bands.filter(b, service_months >= b.service_months).map(b, b.days)) > 0 ? first(bands.filter(b, service_months >= b.service_months).map(b, b.days)) : 0.0

name: Maternity leave extension (without pay)
authority: RA 11210 s.3 (https://lawphil.net/statutes/repacts/ra2019/ra_11210_2019.html): after the 105 days the mother may extend her leave by thirty days without pay, on notice at least forty-five days before the leave ends (the employee’s notice). Metered per pregnancy (`facts.event_id`).

name: Allocated maternity leave (unmarried father or alternate caregiver)
eligibility: has(entry.event_kind) && entry.event_kind in ["BIRTH", "MISCARRIAGE", "EMERGENCY_TERMINATION"] && has(entry.facts) && has(entry.facts.allocation_recipient) && entry.facts.allocation_recipient in ["FATHER", "ALTERNATE_CAREGIVER"] && !(entry.facts.allocation_recipient == "FATHER" && employee.gender == "MALE" && employee.marital_status == "MARRIED") && has(entry.facts.maternity_days_allocated) && double(entry.facts.maternity_days_allocated) > 0.0 && (!has(entry.days) || entry.days <= min(double(entry.facts.maternity_days_allocated), 7.0))
authority: RA 11210 s.6 (https://lawphil.net/statutes/repacts/ra2019/ra_11210_2019.html, read 2026-10-07): the mother may "allocate up to seven (7) days of said benefits to the child’s father, whether or not the same is married to the female worker: Provided, That in the death, absence, or incapacity of the former, the benefit may be allocated to an alternate caregiver who may be a relative within the fourth degree of consanguinity or the current partner of the female worker sharing the same household", on written notice to both employers, "over and above" RA 8187. This class takes the allocated days for a recipient other than a married father (who takes them on PATERNITY_LEAVE with his RA 8187 seven): entry facts `allocation_recipient` (FATHER or ALTERNATE_CAREGIVER) and `maternity_days_allocated` (customer input, from the mother’s written notice), at most seven a birth, miscarriage or emergency termination; with pay, like the paternity days.
